name: CHEMICAL SYMBOLS
clue: Its symbol W comes from Wolfram, its German name; no metal melts at a higher temperature

name: MIDDLE OF NOWHERE
clue: Nicknamed for a Jules Verne captain, this oceanic 'pole of inaccessibility' is where space agencies aim their retiring spacecraft.

name: LOGO LEGENDS
clue: The dribbling silhouette in the NBA's logo was modeled on this Lakers guard nicknamed 'Mr. Clutch'

name: FIRST EMPERORS
clue: After unifying China in 221 B.C., he standardized script, coins, and axle widths; thousands of terracotta soldiers guard his tomb.

name: LINES OF LATITUDE
clue: It's the only country on Earth crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn

name: CELL BIOLOGY
clue: These energy-producing organelles carry their own DNA, a genome you inherit only from your mother

name: BELOW SEA LEVEL
clue: The shores of this hypersaline lake, bordered by Israel and Jordan, are the lowest dry land on Earth

name: RING RECORDS
clue: In 1956 this heavyweight champion retired with a perfect 49-0 record, a mark no heavyweight titleholder has matched

name: CARBON COPIES
clue: Like diamond, this soft gray mineral that fills pencils is an allotrope of pure carbon

name: OVER BEFORE LUNCH
clue: History's shortest recorded war, in 1896, lasted under 40 minutes and pitted Britain against this island sultanate off East Africa.

name: THE PERIODIC TABLE
clue: Element 98, first created in 1950 at a university cyclotron, takes its name from the state where it was made

name: FINAL EPISODES
clue: Over 100 million Americans watched 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen,' the 1983 finale of this Korean War sitcom

name: WORTH ITS WEIGHT
clue: Harvested from crocus stigmas at roughly 150 flowers per gram, this spice has long rivaled gold as the world's costliest.

name: AMERICAN ARCHITECTURE
clue: His only major New York City building, a spiraling Fifth Avenue museum, opened months after his death in 1959

name: MAJOR TRADITIONS
clue: Unlike golf's other three majors, this tournament returns to the very same course every year

name: DAYS OF THE WEEK
clue: Thursday belongs to the thunder god Thor; this day of the week honors his one-eyed father

name: WORLD WAR II
clue: Clouds over the primary target of Kokura diverted the second atomic bomb to this city in August 1945

name: THE $7.2 MILLION QUESTION
clue: Critics branded the 1867 Alaska purchase this Secretary of State's 'folly'; he had survived an assassination attempt the night Lincoln was shot.

name: OPENING SENTENCES
clue: 'Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way' opens this Tolstoy novel

name: STELLAR NEIGHBORS
clue: This red dwarf, with a name meaning 'nearest,' is the closest star to our sun

name: SEVEN WONDERS
clue: Of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, it's the only one still largely standing today

name: MEDICAL IMMORTALITY
clue: Cancer cells taken from this Virginia woman without her consent in 1951 became the first immortal human cell line, called HeLa.

name: COLD WAR CHESS
clue: In Reykjavik in 1972, this American ended a 24-year Soviet grip on the world chess championship

name: ISLAND NATIONS
clue: Earth's fourth-largest island is the biggest occupied entirely by a single country that shares its name

name: HIGH & DRY
clue: Astronomers prize the cloudless skies over this Chilean desert, the driest non-polar place on Earth and home to the ALMA observatory.

name: AGE OF EXPLORATION
clue: After Magellan died in the Philippines, this Basque navigator sailed the Victoria home, completing the first circumnavigation in 1522

name: PLANETARY NAMES
clue: Alone among the eight planets, this one takes its name from Greek rather than Roman mythology

name: UNCONQUERED
clue: Its crushing 1896 victory over Italy at Adwa let this highland empire stay independent throughout the Scramble for Africa.

name: THE CONSTITUTION
clue: It's the only constitutional amendment ratified specifically to repeal an earlier amendment

name: SHOT IN THE ARM
clue: Noticing that milkmaids who caught cowpox never got smallpox, this Gloucestershire doctor performed the first vaccination in 1796.
